Action Plan:
1) Begin NSAID therapy for suspected left elbow bursitis: Ibuprofen 400 mg orally twice daily after meals; monitor for gastric symptoms; discontinue if heartburn occurs.
2) Arrange home blood testing to evaluate for inflammatory/infectious/autoimmune causes: order inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, and gout/CPPD assessment; instructions and forms to be mailed to the patient; expect results in ~5–6 days.
3) Schedule a follow-up appointment (in-person or via telehealth) to review exam findings and blood test results and to reassess the elbow; follow-up timing to be arranged after results are available; patient may request earlier assessment if symptoms worsen.
4) Educate patient on red-flag signs requiring urgent evaluation: if the elbow becomes very red, very painful, or if redness spreads quickly, contact us for an urgent video/phone assessment.
5) Administrative notes: Forms and follow-up logistics to be arranged by clinic staff; Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: New swelling of the left elbow noticed about 1 week ago. Not painful overall; area is slightly warm; patient senses some intra-articular fluid. Function preserved with normal movement.
- History: Prior history of osteoarthritis (GP diagnosed several years ago). No prior elbow swelling. No known elbow injury. Family history not clearly positive for rheumatologic disease.
- PMH: Osteoarthritis. Allergies: peanuts.
- Medications: None regularly.
- Social history: Desk-based job; exercises (runs 2–3 times per week).
- Allergies: Peanuts (anaphylaxis not documented).
- Additional notes: No reported systemic symptoms (fever, weight loss) or other joint involvement.

Objective:
- Left elbow swelling present; area slightly warm.
- Skin around swelling dry.
- Elbow movement preserved; no gross deformity described.
- Palpation: mild tenderness adjacent to swelling; no marked tenderness over tendon/nerve.
- No acute distress; no clear signs of septic infection at this time (no extensive redness, fever, or purulent drainage described).

Assessment & Plan:
1) Issue 1: Olecranon bursitis (aseptic inflammatory bursitis) of the left elbow
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Olecranon bursitis (aseptic) — High likelihood.
   - Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript and DDx):
     - Osteoarthritis with elbow effusion — Medium likelihood.
     - Inflammatory/autoimmune arthritis (e.g., rheumatoid or other inflammatory arthritis) — Medium likelihood.
     - Crystal arthropathy (gout or CPPD) — Medium likelihood.
     - Septic arthritis — Low likelihood (not septic now; monitor for red flags).
   - Investigations planned: Blood tests to assess inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatologic antibodies, and gout/CPPD screening.
   - Treatment planned: Ibuprofen 400 mg PO twice daily after meals; continue unless adverse GI effects occur.
   - Referrals: None at this time.

2) Issue 2: (No separate clinical issue identified requiring separate management beyond the above plan; ongoing OA with intermittent joint symptoms acknowledged)
   - Assessment: Existing osteoarthritis acknowledged; no acute management change beyond current plan unless tests suggest a separate inflammatory process.

Investigations planned for Issue 1:
- Full blood screen: inflammatory markers (e.g., CRP/ESR), infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, and gout/CPPD assessment.
- Expected timeline: Results available in ~5–6 days; blood samples to be collected via home-visit or clinic.

Treatment planned for Issue 1:
- Ibuprofen 400 mg PO twice daily after meals; stop if heartburn occurs.
- Follow-up appointment to review results and reassess the elbow (in-person or telehealth).

Relevant referrals for Issue 1:
- None at this time.

Quality checks (document quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements: None critical identified; allergies and regular medications documented; no vitals recorded (no vitals were provided in transcript).
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: No conflicts noted.
- Transcript quality: Clear overall; no major inaudible segments affecting key facts.
- Verbal consent statement: Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
